clue.text: The women's quarters are breaking the king!

indicators.note: the word are breaks into the king's letters, splitting them apart from inside

parts.note: HM stands for His Majesty, the king
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the women of the palace are defying or ruining their king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts ARE inside HM, the abbreviation for His Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: In a traditional Muslim household the harem is the secluded part of the house reserved for wives and female relatives.

clue.text: It brings tots up to the right level

definitions.text: It brings tots up to the right level

parts.words: It brings tots up to the right level
parts.note: sounds like an educational aim, but describes raised seating that lifts toddlers to table height

explanation.surface: A teaching method that raises small children to the expected standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat with long legs lets a toddler eat at the family table.

clue.text: Coming early, preferably before it ends

indicators.note: the word is stopped before its last letter is reached

parts.note: rather means preferably

explanation.surface: Someone would rather arrive early, before the event finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before it ends' drops the final R of RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old poetic word for early in the season or day.

clue.text: One shipmate is holding the painter

annotationWithheld.why: 'One shipmate is holding the painter' (printed so on the scan): MATISSE needs I and SS inside MATE, so the one word 'shipmate' would have to give both SS (ship) and MATE
annotationWithheld.clue: One shipmate is holding the painter

clue.text: A player who can flourish

parts.note: reads like a performer who thrives, but a flourish is also a fanfare blown on a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A sportsman or actor with the talent to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician on a brass horn sounds the fanfare called a flourish.

clue.text: Volunteers to turn up dreary jacket

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for dreary is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: drab means dreary

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers arrive wearing a dull coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses DRAB to BARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic or short coat, as worn by heralds.

clue.text: University supported by Elysian assembly with some apprehension

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter sits on top of the rest, held up by it
the letters of Elysian are assembled into a new order

explanation.surface: A college backed by a gathering of the blessed views things nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting anxiously, with some nervous worry, is acting uneasily.

clue.text: Chicken soup's cooked at home

indicators.note: the letters of soup's are cooked up into a new order

parts.note: soup's here stands for soup is, so its S counts
in means at home

explanation.surface: Home-made chicken soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A poussin is a very young chicken raised for the table.

clue.text: His animal figure, say, may be in a box

definitions.text: His animal figure, say, may be in a box

parts.words: His animal figure, say, may be in a box
parts.note: suggests a toy kept in a box, but box is the shrub clipped into animal shapes

explanation.surface: A craftsman's animal model is packed in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener who clips hedges such as box into ornamental shapes practises topiary.

clue.text: Loosen girth properly

indicators.note: the letters of girth are loosened and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to slacken a saddle strap correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a thing correctly is doing it right.

clue.text: Acquire an eating place with easy access

parts.note: to acquire something is to get it
the indefinite article, here A
a table is where one eats

explanation.surface: Booking a seat in a restaurant that is easy to get into.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reachable or obtainable without difficulty is easy to get at.

clue.text: Get off line from a Continental tee

parts.note: UN is French for 'a', a Continental word
a golf tee is a small peg

explanation.surface: A golfer abroad teeing off from the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'line' is a washing line: to take clothes off it is to remove the pegs.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the clothes pegs takes washing down from the line.

clue.text: Can't be ruffled — like a stonewaller?

definitions.meaning: said of fabric treated so it will not wrinkle
a stonewalling cricket batsman stays at the crease and resists getting out

explanation.surface: Describing an unflappable person who blocks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line where the batsman stands; a stonewaller bats defensively for hours, refusing to be dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated fabric resists wrinkles; a defensive batsman holds the batting line against bowlers.

clue.text: Gets blown up for sleeping on

definitions.text: Gets blown up for sleeping on

parts.words: Gets blown up for sleeping on
parts.note: sounds like someone scolded for dozing, but describes an inflatable mattress

explanation.surface: Someone is shouted at for falling asleep on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress is pumped full of air before one lies on it.

clue.text: Proving wrong about using one's head

parts.note: re means about, concerning
butting is striking with the head

explanation.surface: Showing someone is mistaken by thinking hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using one's head' looks like thinking but means headbutting.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute, disproving a claim.

clue.text: Looking hastily for a fag-end at school

parts.note: the end of the word fag is its last letter, G
Lancing is a public school in Sussex

explanation.surface: A pupil furtively looking for a cigarette butt at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places G next to LANCING. LANCING College is an English boarding school; a fag is also British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief quick look is a glance, so glancing is looking briefly.

clue.text: Little pig progressed gradually, being of the highest quality

parts.note: a gilt is a young female pig
edged means moved forward slowly

explanation.surface: A piglet inching forward proves first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: GILT-EDGED also describes safe British government stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the very best, most reliable sort is what gilt-edged means.

clue.text: Word books are a sure hit as a diversion

indicators.note: the letters are diverted from their order, making a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Dictionaries make a popular pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a diversion' rearranges A SURE HIT; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of synonyms are reference books of words.

clue.text: It's a mistake to split a precious stone — it becomes worthless

indicators.note: the stone's letters are split apart by the mistake set inside them

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone
bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: A jeweller's blunder in cutting a gem destroys its value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to split' is the container signal; 'bish' is British slang for a blunder, little known outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy, of no value, is what rubbishy means.

clue.text: Arrangement of ""The Flowers that Bloom in the Spring''?

definitions.text: Arrangement of ""The Flowers that Bloom in the Spring''?

parts.words: Arrangement of ""The Flowers that Bloom in the Spring''?
parts.note: reads like a musical arrangement of the song from The Mikado, set in Japan, but means arranging the flowers themselves

explanation.surface: A new orchestration of a Gilbert and Sullivan song.
explanation.walkthrough: The song comes from Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado, set in Japan, which points to a Japanese art.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of formal flower arrangement.

clue.text: Trade association's vehicle has phone

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: A business group's car is fitted with a telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is an alliance of firms fixing prices or output.

clue.text: Settle a source of righteous anger perhaps

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word's source is where it starts, its first letter
perhaps signals the letters of anger may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Calm a burst of justified fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a matter is to organise or fix it.

clue.text: Grease monkey with lots of bottle?

definitions.text: Grease monkey with lots of bottle?

parts.words: Grease monkey with lots of bottle?
parts.note: a brave young mechanic, read literally, is a vehicle lad, which names a big glass bottle

explanation.surface: A courageous young mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage, and a grease monkey is a car boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large bottle, often in a protective frame, for acids.

clue.text: Damage main span over the Thames

parts.note: to batter is to damage by blows
the main is a poetic word for the sea
a bridge spans a gap

explanation.surface: Harm done to the main span of a London river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like an adjective for the span, but is the sea. The answer is the London crossing between Chelsea and Battersea.
explanation.definitionFit: That London crossing stands across the river, linking Chelsea to the south bank.

clue.text: Bishop bound, I hear, to call

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: says the word for bound is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A churchman jumps to answer a summons.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone by pager is to send them an electronic signal.

clue.text: The housewife's modern spinning wheel

parts.note: suggests an updated spinning wheel for yarn, but means a machine spinning wet laundry

explanation.surface: A homemaker's up-to-date spinning wheel for wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin machine whirls water out of washed clothes.

clue.text: She takes part of hysterical maid

indicators.note: she is only a portion of the following letters, lying within them

explanation.surface: A woman joins in with an overwrought servant's hysterics.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for any 'she' in crosswords.

clue.text: Straightening out firm

explanation.surface: Correcting a stubborn company.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking out a curve straightens; an inflexible, determined person is also described this way.

clue.text: Name a big town after boxer for aggressiveness

indicators.note: the clue's earlier words come after the boxer in the answer

parts.note: a pug is a boxer, short for pugilist
taken as written
a city is a big town

explanation.surface: Naming a city after a fighter as a tribute to its spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Combative belligerence, a readiness to fight, is pugnacity.

clue.text: English king, bloodstained, fell

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
something bloodstained is red

explanation.surface: An English monarch, covered in blood, fell in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall is to sin or go astray, which is to have done wrong.
